items.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven intrusion ecosystem run by affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups. Central to the operation is an "Autonomous Red Team Kill Chain Framework" referred to as Phantom. The threat actor is assessed to be Russian-speaking and functions both as an intrusion and data-extortion operator, as well as an infrastructure provider supporting different partners across the ransomware ecosystem. "The operators exploited edge and remote-access systems at scale, including FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, cPanel and VPN gateways," SOCRadar said. "They used AI-managed knowledge bases to track victims, stolen credentials and campaign progress." A notable aspect that defines the campaign is its "AI-executed, human-approved operating structure" in which a human operator provides a victim-specific prompt and reviews every step, while the intrusions themselves are executed through OpenCode with OpenRouter-hosted commercial models.

items.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a large-scale campaign that has targeted exposed network edge devices such as Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect firewalls. "Artifacts from this investigation also indicate that operators in this campaign have obtained access to numerous organizations worldwide, and have attempted to further compromise some victims, resulting in persistent remote access and data exfiltration," according to a joint investigation published by Group-IB and NyxLab. The widespread exploitation activity has been attributed to a threat actor known as k0t, who also goes by the aliases CryptoFeel, Member19, and QazWsxShop. The cybercriminal actor was first seen in the wild on October 22, 2025.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
items.summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw and released fixes on October 21, and applications that decode untrusted Brotli data should update. Imperva's test did not succeed on every attempt, and code execution took several tries in its Linux arm64 setup. The result covers that one build and application setup, with other architectures and the 22.x and 26.x lines not tested. On the fixed release, 24.22.1, the same data was rejected, and no code ran. The demonstration goes beyond the first public proof of concept, which achieved code execution only on a deliberately weakened test build. On a standard build, that proof of concept's author reported a crash and a limited read of process memory, not code execution, and said a working attack on a normal build was not achieved.

HPE Networking has released patches for the HPE Networking Wireless Operating Systems (AOS-8 and AOS-10) for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways, and Access Points that address multiple security vulnerabilities.

Affected Products

These vulnerabilities affect the following HPE Networking Wireless Operating Systems (AOS-8 and AOS-10) software versions unless specifically noted otherwise in the details section:

HPE Networking

Mobility Conductors
Mobility Controllers
Mobility Gateways (Managed by HPE Networking Central)
AOS-10 Access Points (AOS-AP)
AOS-8 Instant Access Points (AOS-IAP)

Affected Software Version(s):

AOS-10.8.x.x: 10.8.1.1 and below
AOS-10.7.x.x: 10.7.2.6 and below
AOS-10.4.x.x: 10.4.1.13 and below
AOS-8.13.x.x: 8.13.3.0 and below
AOS-8.10.x.x: 8.10.0.23 and below

Any hardware, Mobility solutions (such as conductors, controllers, and gateways), access points, or virtual machines (VMs) compatible with the affected versions are vulnerable.

These vulnerabilities were generally discovered by internal security research at HPE Networking. HPE Networking is not aware of any public discussion or exploit code that targets the listed vulnerabilities as of the release date of this advisory. Customers are strongly urged to patch their instances due to the complexity, breadth, and impact of these vulnerabilities.

Workaround

To minimize the likelihood of an attacker exploiting these vulnerabilities, HPE Networking recommends that the CLI and web-based management interfaces be restricted to a dedicated layer 2 segment/VLAN and/or controlled by firewall policies at layer 3 and above along with accounting controls for tracking and logging user activities and resource usage.

items.title: Waiting for the PHP2Shell Onslaught as POCs Proliferate
items.summary: Cyberdefenders are bracing for breakthroughs in weaponized exploits targeting just-patched vulnerabilities in widely used PHP code. The flaws could enable attackers to take control of any server and underlying device running PHP as well as stored data. No in-the-wild exploits for what's being dubbed PHP2Shell have yet been confirmed. The Dutch National Cyber Security Center reported Thursday that it's "currently investigating initial signs of successful exploitation" and urged organizations to immediately apply patched updates

items.title: Kolmas haavoittuvuus PHP:ssä, päivitys tulossa myöhemmin
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Workaround, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: CVE-2026-115560, Summary: Informational advisory: Session upload progress We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector. This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed. The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and application code. An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release. See also: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/urgent-php-warns-of-another-unpatched.html

items.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
items.summary: The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch. PHP is an open-source web development language used by nearly 70% of all websites on the Internet. According to VirusTotal estimates, more than 5.1 million PHP hosts are exposed online, and roughly 3.8 million have at least one port open to attacks. According to a Friday advisory, this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-115560) can only be exploited when targeting systems "with an unusual combination of configuration and application code."

items.title: Fortinet Releases Security Hardening Release for Multiple Products
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: Fortinet has released a coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer following recent releases from FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator. They strongly urge every customer to plan and promptly complete these upgrades as soon as the releases are available, prioritizing internet-facing devices. These releases include fixes to address vulnerabilities identified through frontier AI-assisted security testing program. Fortinet would like to thank Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX for their collaboration throughout this process. Customers are recommended to treat this release as a priority change rather than a routine maintenance cycle. Four factors drive this urgency: Criticality of fixes: These releases include critical and high-severity fixes. Faster weaponization: AI tools can now help adversaries reverse-engineer patches and build working exploits in hours or days, rather than weeks. Patch diffing risk: Once updates are public, the fixes themselves reveal where changes were made, exposing a potential system weakness. Unpatched devices then become easier targets for attackers. Chaining of vulnerabilities: AI has the ability to link seemingly unrelated lower severity vulnerabilities together to achieve a more severe, exploitable vulnerability. Tehe recommendation is to apply temporary mitigations, including limiting exposure by managing devices out of band, moving resources behind VPN or SASE where feasible, and applying virtual patches until the patching can be prioritized. See also: https://www.reddit.com/r/fortinet/comments/1xct1c4/anyone_ran_the_new_update_through_ai_and_compared/?solution=b8ec52f7c4a8fc66b8ec52f7c4a8fc66&js_challenge=1&jsc_token=2824be10929bdc604753c70a67a1c3317b245a2078a27b43c1df4986166d9c03&jsc_orig_r

items.title: UK threatens subsea cable saboteurs with 14 years behind bars
items.summary: Britain is threatening subsea cable saboteurs with up to 14 years in prison and unlimited fines, having apparently decided that Victorian-era laws aren't quite up to the job of keeping Russian submarines away from critical infrastructure. The government on Thursday set out plans to overhaul legislation dating back to 1885 and introduce tougher penalties for damaging the underwater cables and pipelines that keep Britain's internet and energy supplies running. According to Whitehall, subsea cables carry around 99 percent of the UK's international data traffic, while underwater pipelines account for 74 percent of its gas supply. Yet much of this infrastructure is protected by laws written when the telegraph was cutting-edge technology. The Submarine Telegraph Act 1885 originally imposed a £100 maximum fine for damaging a cable through culpable negligence. That might have been a reasonable deterrent back then, but it's unlikely to give today's would-be saboteurs much pause. Under the proposals, those who intentionally damage critical subsea energy or telecoms infrastructure could face up to 14 years behind bars. The proposals also set tougher penalties, including unlimited fines, for reckless or negligent damage. Subsea telecoms operators would face new legal duties to identify and manage security risks, while ministers would gain powers to direct companies and cable repair providers to take action where necessary and proportionate to protect national security. The government also wants to regulate fiber-optic sensing technology, which uses subsea cables to detect activity at sea but could pose a security risk if sensitive data falls into hostile hands.

items.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
items.summary: eMudhra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business. V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers.

items.title: Merkittävät kansalaisiin vaikuttavat järjestelmät korjattu
items.summary: Valtionhallinnon verkkopalveluiden korjauspäivitykset ovat edenneet käyttökatkojen jäljiltä. – Merkittävät kansalaisiin vaikuttavat järjestelmät on korjattu, kertoi Valtion tieto- ja viestintätekniikkakeskus Valtorin tietohallinnon ylijohtaja Hannu Naumanen STT:lle perjantaina. Suuri joukko verkkopalveluita oli keskiviikkona nurin ympäri maailmaa PHP-ohjelmointikielestä löytyneiden haavoittuvuuksien vuoksi.
